column1: # snapshot: same-change identity refreshes over the frozen residual prose-pin manifest
# frozen-manifest: .devflow/logs/residual-prose-retirement-manifest.tsv
# consumed-by: lib/test/test_residual_prose_retirement_manifest.py, class
#   ResidualRequiredCopyRetirementManifestTests -- the class whose name reads
#   "RequiredCopy" but which loads the residual-PROSE manifest named above. Go by
#   the manifest path, not the class name.
# contract: each row declares one RETAIN_BOUNDARY identity frozen in that manifest, and the
#   assertion name the tree now carries for it. The manifest row itself is never edited: its
#   identity set is pinned to the base revision's committed pin-corpus inventory, so an edit
#   there would break the historical partition permanently. A row is admitted only when the
#   old identity is gone from the tree and the new one is present, so a rename and its
#   re-freeze land in the same commit and a refresh cannot outlive the rename it records.
# lifetime: a row lives exactly as long as the rename it records. The arm requiring `old` to name
#   a RETAIN_BOUNDARY identity of the frozen manifest is anchored to that immutable snapshot and is
#   fixed forever -- which is why regenerating the live census .devflow/logs/pin-corpus-inventory.tsv
#   never disturbs a row. The two LIVENESS arms (old identity gone from the tree, refreshed identity
#   present in it) are re-checked against the CURRENT TREE every run, so the row does need
#   maintenance:
#     * renaming the same pin again UPDATES this row's new_assertion_name in place -- never add a
#       second row, because `old` would then have to name the intermediate name, which the frozen
#       manifest does not carry;
#     * renaming the pin BACK to its frozen name DELETES the row, because a self-mapping row is
#       rejected and both liveness arms would otherwise go red;
#     * changing the pin's LITERAL or RESOLVED TARGET is out of scope for this ledger and is never
#       expressed by editing a row. The six identity cells are the OLD identity, and the refresh
#       rewrites assertion_name alone, so editing `literal`/`resolved_target` makes `old` absent
#       from the frozen manifest while leaving it unedited makes the refreshed identity absent from
#       the tree -- both red, with no valid repair. Such a change retires the frozen identity and is
#       handled by the manifest/inventory retirement protocol in CONTRIBUTING.md, not here.
